claims.claim: USGS filmed lava spattering at fissure 18 around 02:00 HST on 16 May 2018.
claims.evidence_note: USGS May 16 video description identifies fissure 18, ~02:00 HST and authentic field audio.

claims.claim: Lower East Rift Zone eruptive fissures began May 3; USGS video near fissure 22 was captured overnight May 22 and posted May 24.
claims.evidence_note: USGS chronology describes May 3 initial eruption and May 24 video page specifies recording May 22.

claims.claim: Fissure 8 lava entered Kapoho Bay late June 3. USGS recorded the resulting ocean entry June 4 at 06:15 and 13:38.
claims.evidence_note: USGS notes entry by June 3 10:30 PM and its two compilation recordings on June 4.

claims.claim: A collapse/explosion event filmed at Kīlauea summit June 30 included rockfall and a small plume; magma withdrawal reduced support at summit.
claims.evidence_note: USGS footage description specifies June 30 at 14:51 HST; uploaded page July 2; explains magma drainage.

claims.claim: Magma propagated eastward along the rift zone before May 3, 2018, as recorded in volcanic and seismic observations.
claims.evidence_note: USGS official 2018 eruption overview: April 30 Puʻuʻōʻō collapse followed by magma dike migration and May 3 initial fissure eruptions.

claims.claim: Lava entering seawater creates a laze plume containing steam, hydrochloric acid, and fine volcanic glass particles; it can irritate lungs, eyes and skin.
claims.evidence_note: USGS 'Kīlauea Volcano Erupts' and Kapoho Bay laze image: laze consists of steam, HCl, and tiny volcanic glass particles with hazardous effects.

claims.claim: Drainage of shallow summit magma reduced support beneath overlying rock, causing repeated collapse at Kīlauea summit.
claims.evidence_note: USGS video detail explains magma draining to East Rift Zone slowly removes support and crater floor collapses incrementally.

claims.claim: Monitoring Kīlauea enabled forecasting of hazardous events and helps scientists explain hazards and risks.
claims.evidence_note: USGS/Neal et al. 2019 describes successful forecasting through careful historical observation and monitoring.
